meta.scope: Finance-specific ML libraries, model zoos, factor libraries and agentic systems not assessed by docs/research/prediction-engine-sweep-2026-09-26.md; judged on independent net-of-cost evidence and on cheap testability in the L40 harness (backend/research/kronos_feature_ic.py).
meta.channels: agent-reach: Exa web search (mcporter exa.web_search_exa), GitHub via gh CLI (repos, issues, search, README, releases), page reads via r.jina.ai and raw.githubusercontent.com. No login-backed platform used.
meta.harness_bar: quintile spread > 33.26 bp, t > 2 across >= 60 sessions, both halves positive, BH q=0.10 over 3 horizons, partial IC given m60 positive with t > 2; costs 16.63 bp round trip; selection sample 2025-09-01..2025-12-31, six decision times, horizons 15/30/60 min.
project_facts_checked: No trained model (lightgbm/xgboost/sklearn) exists anywhere in backend/research/*.py; every prior trial used hand-coded rules or a foundation model (L40).
Kite order-book sampler: 5 levels at ~30 s (prereg-orderbook.md, Amendment 1), recording since 2026-09-24, so ~5 sessions exist.
None of the names below appears in docs/research/*.md except qlib (literature sweep row: CSI300 LightGBM IR 2.00 gross -> 1.44 with cost, backtest only).

candidates.name: Microsoft Qlib: LightGBM on Alpha158 (and the deep zoo: TFT, HIST, TRA, ADD, IGMTF, KRNN; Alpha360)
candidates.predicts: Cross-sectional excess return of each stock over the next N bars (benchmark label: Ref($close,-2)/Ref($close,-1)-1, i.e. next-day close-to-close); the high-frequency example predicts the next 1-minute trend with the same Alpha158 handler.
candidates.horizon: Daily in the benchmarks; 1-minute in examples/highfreq (workflow_config_High_Freq_Tree_Alpha158.yaml).
candidates.data_needed: OHLCV bars only (Alpha158 = 158 hand-made rolling price/volume expressions; Alpha360 = the raw last-60-bar OHLCV window). HIST additionally needs a stock-to-concept (industry/business) matrix that does not exist for NSE.
candidates.runs_on_project_data: Yes. Daily bhavcopies load through dump_bin; an IN-region Yahoo collector was merged in 2021 (PR #513). For 5-minute bars either register a custom frequency in Qlib's bin format (native calendars are 'day' and '1min'; untested here) or port the 158 expressions in qlib/contrib/data/loader.py (Alpha158DL.get_feature_config) to pandas with windows in bars. No new downloads.
candidates.training: Yes. LightGBM: minutes on the Mac CPU. TRA/HIST/IGMTF/ADD: tens of minutes to hours on the RTX 3060 Ti. TFT example pins Python 3.6-3.7 and CUDA 10.0 (examples/benchmarks/TFT/README.md) - effectively unrunnable on current tooling.
issues: #1668 (open, 2023-10): run_all_model.py cannot reproduce the published benchmark table; a second user confirms.
#2029 (open, 2025-10): KRNN gives poor, non-improving scores on the shipped config; the published KRNN row is itself negative (AR -4.65%, IR -0.54).
#1276 (closed, 2022): HIST shipped without the code that generates stock2concept data.
#1774 (closed, 2024): question whether DDG-DA's proxy-model normalisation uses future mean/std; answered as train-only.
No open issue reports look-ahead in Alpha158 itself; the label uses Ref(close,-2)/Ref(close,-1) by design (buy at the next close).

independent_evidence.claim: Alpha158/LightGBM on a US universe with 2+2 bp costs and three expanding-window folds: mean fold IC +0.0069 but mean Rank IC -0.0053, not positive in every fold; the author's own gate returned RESEARCH_ONLY; universe survivorship-biased. Headline 'excess return with cost 35-80%' is a Qlib portfolio simulation the author refuses to treat as evidence.

Vendor's own high-frequency benchmark (Chinese 1-minute bars, Alpha158 + LightGBM): IC 0.0349, Rank IC 0.0435, long-short average return 0.000074 (0.74 bp per period), long-short Sharpe 0.27, no costs.

Vendor's own daily CSI300 benchmark, mean of 20 seeds: LightGBM Alpha158 IC 0.0399, Rank IC 0.0482, AR 12.8%, IR 1.57; deep zoo rows sit within +/-0.01 IC of LightGBM (HIST 0.0522, IGMTF 0.0480, TRA 0.0440-0.0485, ADD 0.0430, TFT 0.0358, KRNN 0.0173 with negative return).
independent_evidence.net_of_cost: Qlib backtest default costs; not independently verified

candidates.indian_or_intraday_evidence: None net of cost. Vendor 1-min CN benchmark is gross and ~0.7 bp per period.
candidates.covered_by_sweep: Partly. Literature sweep row (CSI300, backtest only). Engine sweep rejected 'ML on OHLCV bars' as a family on external evidence, but the project has never trained any model on its own bars; trials 41-116 were hand-coded rules.
candidates.how: One pre-registered look in the L40 harness, not a trial: port the Alpha158 expression list to the Kite 5-minute bars (windows in bars), train one LightGBM regressor per horizon (targets = the harness's 15/30/60-minute next-bar-open-to-close returns, cross-sectionally rank-normalised) on 2024-09..2025-08-15 with a 5-session purge, freeze, then score the three forecasts at the six decision times on the 2025-09..12 selection sample exactly as L40 scores Kronos. Family of 3, BH q=0.10, partial IC given m60. Skip TFT/HIST/TRA/KRNN/ADD/IGMTF as separate looks: their own tables show no material gain over LightGBM, KRNN is negative, HIST needs concept data. Expected result: null (vendor's own 1-min number is 0.7 bp gross against a 16.63 bp round trip).

candidates.name: Intraday market-return predictability from the lagged high-frequency factor zoo (Aleti, Bollerslev, Siggaard; Management Science 2025) - a factor-library method, not a repo
candidates.licence: Paper; online appendix and data files at the DOI. No maintained code repo found.
candidates.predicts: Time-series (not cross-sectional) intraday return of the aggregate market from lagged intraday returns on 200+ characteristic-sorted factor portfolios, regularised by ridge/LASSO/elastic net/boosting; continuous vs jump increments separated.
candidates.data_needed: Intraday returns on many characteristic-sorted portfolios, which requires stock-level intraday bars plus the characteristics (from daily data) to build them.
candidates.runs_on_project_data: Partly. NIFTY 100 5-minute bars plus bhavcopy-derived characteristics (size, 12-1 momentum, realised vol, turnover, beta) can build a few dozen intraday factor-portfolio return series; the 200-factor zoo cannot be replicated. Target would be NIFTY (futures ~6-7 bp) rather than single stocks.
candidates.training: Yes, small: penalised regressions, seconds on CPU.

independent_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed (Management Science 71(9), 2025): SPY intraday strategy on the model's forecasts gives an annualised transaction-cost-adjusted Sharpe of 1.37 and a Fama-French six-factor alpha of 20.83% out of sample, against 0.09 intraday Sharpe for SPY itself; gains concentrate in high-uncertainty periods and a few liquidity/tail-risk factors.

candidates.only_evidence_is_own_backtest: Authors' own, but peer-reviewed, out of sample and cost-adjusted; no third-party replication found.
candidates.covered_by_sweep: No. The sweep's 'flow and calendar' row (L32, +0.70 bp) is last-30-minute momentum, not cross-sectional factor lead-lag into the index.
candidates.how: Not a fit for the L40 harness (which ranks stocks); it needs its own pre-registration with a market-timing target (NIFTY futures or NIFTYBEES intraday return over 30/60 minutes), a fixed small factor set buildable from project data, an expanding-window ridge fit, and a hurdle of the futures round trip plus a Bonferroni family of 1. Do it only if the owner opens an index-timing family; the mechanism (slow-moving capital in a 200-factor zoo) may not exist with ~20 NIFTY 100 factor portfolios.

candidates.name: HKUDS Vibe-Trading - Alpha Zoo v1 (qlib158 port, alpha101, gtja191, academic; 452 alphas) inside an LLM trading agent
candidates.licence: MIT (the qlib158 port is an Apache-2.0 port of Qlib's Alpha158 with the upstream SHA pinned)
candidates.predicts: Nothing by itself: the zoo is a pandas factor library plus a 'bench any zoo on your universe' CLI; the surrounding product is an LLM agent (v0.1.16 on 2026-09-29).
candidates.horizon: Daily formulas (Alpha158 windows in days; Alpha101 and GTJA191 are daily formulas).
candidates.data_needed: OHLCV; 19 Alpha101 formulas need sector tags.
candidates.runs_on_project_data: Probably, as a library: pass the 5-minute bars as the frame and the window units become bars. NOT verified here; the intraday semantics of daily formulas are the user's problem.
issues: 104 issue/PR hits for leak/lookahead in five months. #1293/#1299/#1304/#1305 (closed 2026-08-31): options signals were filled at the same-day close and HV warm-up used look-ahead. #1578 (open, 2026-09-24): Carhart momentum leaked today's price into the skip-month return. #1613/#1618 (open, 2026-09-27): add a warning when a backtest window lies inside the LLM's training data. These are the repo fixing its own leakage, which is the right direction but also the record.
Release notes say the zoo is 'lookahead-banned at the operator layer' and 'registry-validated'; not independently checked.
candidates.covered_by_sweep: No (repo created 2026-04; name absent from both sweeps). Its agent layer belongs to the LLM-agent family the sweep rejected.
candidates.recommendation: test only as the factor implementation for candidate 1 (skip the agent)
candidates.how: If the qlib158 module computes Alpha158 on an arbitrary OHLCV frame without Qlib's bin store, use it (Apache-2.0, pinned to upstream) as the feature step of the LightGBM look instead of hand-porting 158 expressions. Verify on 20 random stock-bars that features at time t are bit-identical with and without later bars present (the L40 stage-0 lookahead proof). Do not run its 'bench any zoo' CLI as a search: 452 alphas x 3 horizons is 1,356 comparisons and would consume the family budget.

candidates.name: DeepLOB, DeepLOB-Attention, TransLOB, TLOB, and the LOBCAST / LOBFrame benchmark frameworks
candidates.licence: DeepLOB none; TransLOB none; TLOB MIT; LOBCAST none; LOBFrame none; lob-deep-learning none
candidates.predicts: 3-class mid-price trend (up/flat/down) k LOB events ahead (k = 1..100 events, i.e. seconds to a few minutes) from the last 100 snapshots of a 10-level book.
candidates.horizon: Event-based, seconds to minutes; far inside one spread at NSE cash costs.
candidates.data_needed: Event-level (every update) 10-level LOB with months of history per stock (DeepLOB: one year of LSE; LOBCAST: LOBSTER 2021-22; TLOB: NASDAQ LOBSTER).
candidates.runs_on_project_data: No. Kite depth is 5 levels sampled every ~30 s (prereg-orderbook.md), recorded since 2026-09-24 (about five sessions). Neither the depth, the cadence nor the history exists.
candidates.training: Yes, from scratch: no pretrained weights transfer across venues. DeepLOB (~60k parameters) trains in hours on an 8 GB GPU; TLOB/TransLOB similar.
issues: DeepLOB repo: 18 open issues, last push 2021, no licence.
DeepLOB's own profit simulation is mid-to-mid with no transaction costs, stated in the paper ('we use mid-prices without transaction costs').

independent_evidence.claim: LOBCAST (Prata et al., Artificial Intelligence Review 2024): 15 re-implemented DL LOB models (incl. DeepLOB, DeepLOB-Attention, TransLOB, BiN-CTABL) all drop sharply from FI-2010 to unseen NASDAQ LOBSTER 2021/2022 data, F1 48-61%; 'not consistently reliable ... inadequate for practical applications in real-world settings'.
independent_evidence.net_of_cost: Profit analysis included; F1 collapse is the headline.

independent_evidence.claim: LOBFrame (Briola et al., 2025, LSE/UCL): on 15 NASDAQ stocks DeepLOB's 'high forecasting power does not necessarily correspond to actionable trading signals'; standard ML metrics overstate usability.
TLOB (Berti et al., 2025): 'existing models fail to generalize across different market conditions and assets'; a plain MLP adapted to LOB beats prior SoTA.

candidates.only_evidence_is_own_backtest: Originals yes; the three independent benchmarks are negative on generalisation.
candidates.indian_or_intraday_evidence: No NSE study found. The sweep's own NSE finding: order-imbalance predictability perishes within 30 minutes.
candidates.covered_by_sweep: DeepLOB named; successors and the two benchmark frameworks were not. Family (order-book microstructure) judged 'not supported', L37 running.
candidates.how: Revisit only if L37 clears its gate AND at least three months of 5-level snapshots exist; then one look with TLOB or DeepLOB retrained on the snapshots, scored at the L40 horizons (15/30/60 min), never at the paper's 10-event horizons. Two independent benchmarks already show these models do not transfer even between US datasets.

candidates.name: Independent pre-registered Kronos studies found on GitHub (not tools; prior evidence for L40)
candidates.licence: kronos-candlecast MIT; OpenAlpha MIT; FineForecast proprietary (personal use); kronos-india MIT
candidates.predicts: Kronos-small/base zero-shot OHLCV paths (candlecast: NSE daily, 30-session horizon; OpenAlpha: 4 US ETFs, 40->12 daily horizon). FineForecast: QLoRA fine-tune of Kronos-base on NSE plus a MASTER-style head ranking Nifty 500 (monthly-style L/S deciles). kronos-india: daily-after-close signal pipeline on 1-minute bars.
candidates.horizon: Daily to 30 sessions (candlecast), 12 days (OpenAlpha); not the L40 intraday horizons.
candidates.data_needed: Daily bars (candlecast, OpenAlpha, FineForecast via yfinance).
candidates.runs_on_project_data: Not relevant; these are results, not tools. candlecast's kronos-calibrate harness reads any sampled-path file and returns fair CRPS/coverage - reusable if L40 ever wants calibration metrics.
candidates.training: None for the two negatives; FineForecast trains LoRA adapters + head on a GPU.

independent_evidence.claim: kronos-candlecast (acceptance rule committed 2026-08-03, grid run five days later): Kronos-small zero-shot on NSE daily bars, 708 rolling windows, 59 tickers, 12 independent dates, 30-member ensembles: fair CRPS 121.87 vs 67.24 for random walk + drift (81% worse), interval score 978 vs 463, 80% intervals cover 41.3% [37.0, 45.6]. Conformal repair does not fix it.

OpenAlpha: Kronos-base zero-shot on 4 US ETFs, 25 origins each, 1,600 generations, two temperatures: median relative skill vs zero-return persistence -0.042 (T=0.6) and -0.084 (T=1.0); origins beating persistence 31%/26% vs 60% required; 0/4 assets; moving-block 95% CI excludes zero on the unfavourable side. Also 12-25% of tokenizer round-trips are structurally invalid candles; repairing them changes forecast error by 0.0.

FineForecast README lists 'Phase 4 walk-forward backtest + transaction-cost L/S portfolio' as complete but publishes no number in the README; licence forbids reuse. kronos-india: 'Results are currently being collected'.

candidates.only_evidence_is_own_backtest: candlecast and OpenAlpha are pre-registered negatives by third parties; FineForecast/kronos-india report nothing.
candidates.covered_by_sweep: No (all four repos post-date or were missed by the 2026-09-26 sweep; Kronos itself was covered: 49.3% direction on NSE index).
candidates.recommendation: not a tool - attach as prior evidence to L40; keep L40 as written
candidates.how: Cite both negatives in the L40 results file. They test daily horizons, so they neither replace nor shorten the intraday look; they lower its prior further. A Kronos fine-tune (FineForecast's shape) would be a later, separate pre-registration and only if L40's zero-shot spread is non-zero but under the bar.
